description: Open Vista: the second of the four stress profiles docs/renderer-upgrade/05-scope-contract.md §45 schedules, and the one the Glowmere density ladder does not cover. The ladder is a closed understorey a few metres deep -- a foreground problem, which is why it loads culling and overdraw. This is the opposite shot: mountainous relief over 1.4 km, thin ground cover, large negative space, and the composition weight pushed into the background band. Same seed, same asset library and same art profile as the rungs, so a difference between this and them is a difference in the shot and not in the content. LOOKED AT, and reported as it is rather than as intended (docs/renderer-upgrade/08-certification.md §4): the frame is sparse ground running out to a distant ridge with a lot of sky, which is the profile -- but the composer still places its foreground hero, so 'almost everything in frame is far away and small' is NOT true of it. 304 visible instances carrying 277,661 submitted triangles is 914 triangles apiece against glowmere-medium's 103, and that ratio is the same fact from the counters' side. It is a genuinely different workload from every rung -- 15.99 ms GPU under a 26.81 ms wall clock, a bottleneck the ladder does not have -- and it is not yet the distant-representation torture case §45 has in mind.

certification.what: Open Vista: long sightlines, mountainous relief, thin cover -- the distant-representation and shadow-cascade profile of §45
certification.declares: The counters below are what this scene submits at the resolution, tier and camera named here. Every one of them is a deterministic function of (recipe, library, seed, camera, resolution) -- the composition is hash-addressed rather than stream-addressed, so it does not drift -- which is why they are checked exactly and the frame times are not checked at all. tools/certify.py renders this file and compares. A counter that has moved is a real change in what the renderer draws, and the diff of this block is the statement of it.
